summary: Yasutaka Muroya works in Indology and philosophy. He has held research associate positions at the University of Vienna (attested 2007), Leipzig University (attested 2015), and the Institute for the Cultural and Intellectual History of Asia (attested 2022).

Yasutoshi Murakami is a Buddhist studies scholar who studied at Tohoku University. He has held posts at Yamaguchi University, Koyasan University, and served as president of the Association of Esoteric Buddhist Studies (attested 2004).
Yawen Yang is a scholar of Buddhist studies who earned an MA at Fo Guang University under the supervision of Yongdong Shi (attested 2009).
Yi-hsun Huang specializes in Buddhist studies and Sinology. She completed her PhD at the University of Virginia under the supervision of Paul Groner and has taught Huidi Zeng.

Yifa is a Buddhist and religious studies scholar. She studied under Hsing Yun, earned degrees from National Taiwan University, the University of Hawaii, and a PhD at Yale under Stanley Weinstein, later holding posts at University of the West and Harvard.

Yigal Bronner is an Indologist who studied at the Hebrew University of Jerusalem (~1988–1994) and the University of Chicago under Sheldon Pollock (~1994–1999). He joined the faculty at the Hebrew University of Jerusalem around 2008.

Yiliang Zhou was a scholar of history, Sinology, and Buddhist studies. He studied at Fu Jen, Yenching, and Harvard Universities, as well as under Yinke Chen, and served as a professor at Peking University from around 1952 to 2001.

Yin Shun was a Buddhist studies scholar who studied under Taixu and at Minnan, Wuchang, NTNU, and Taisho University. He held teaching posts at Minnan, Wuchang, Shandao Temple, and NCKU, and served as president of the Hong Kong Buddhist Association.

Ying-shih Yü was a scholar of Sinology, history, and philosophy who studied at CUHK, Kansai University, and Harvard. He held professorships at the University of Michigan (~1962–1966), Yale University (~1977–1987), and Princeton University (~1987–2021).
Yingguang Qu was a scholar in Buddhist studies and Tibetology who studied under Nordan Hutuktu in 1926 and Bai Puren in 1929.

Yinke Chen was a historian, Sinologist, and Buddhist studies scholar who studied at Fudan, Humboldt, Zurich, Sciences Po, and Harvard. He held major posts at Tsinghua University (~1925–1938), Peking University (~1946–1948), and Sun Yat-sen University (~1949–1969).
Yiu Wing Chan is a scholar of Buddhist studies who completed a PhD at the University of Hong Kong under the supervision of K. L. Dhammajoti (graduated by 2013).

Yiu-ming Fung is a scholar in philosophy and Buddhist studies who earned his PhD from The Chinese University of Hong Kong in 1984. He served as Acting Head of the Division of Humanities at HKUST (attested 2008–2009).

Yohei Kawajiri is a scholar of Indology and philosophy. He has held positions as a research associate at Chikushi Jogakuen University (attested 2008–2013) and as a JSPS special research fellow (attested 2011).
Yoichi Fukuda is a scholar of Tibetology and Buddhist studies. He served as a full-time researcher at Toyo Bunko (attested 1986–1991) and as a professor at Otani University (attested 2003 and 2015).
Yong Hua Shi is a Buddhist studies scholar who earned a Master of Arts degree at the International Buddhist College under the supervision of Tilak Kariyawasam and Fa Qing (attested 2014).

Yongey Mingyur Rinpoche is a figure in Buddhist studies and Tibetology. He studied under Nyoshul Khenpo Jamyang Dorje (~1987–1999), Khenchen Thrangu Rinpoche, and Trulshik Rinpoche, and has taught Cortland Dahl and Adam Pearcey.
Yongshan He specializes in Buddhist studies and Sinology. He studied at McMaster University under the doctoral supervision of James A. Benn, and also studied with Shayne Clarke and Mark Rowe.

Yongtong Tang was a scholar of Buddhist studies, philosophy, and Sinology. He studied at Tsinghua University (~1912–1916) and Harvard University (~1918–1922), and served in the Philosophy Department at Peking University in 1949.

Yonten Gyatso was a scholar of Tibetology and history. He earned a Geshé degree at Drepung Gomang Dratsang and a diplôme at École Pratique des Hautes Études, where he later served as a research advisor for Tibetan Studies.
